name: Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) - 50-year interest-free loans, FY2026-27 iteration
agency: Department of Expenditure (PF-S Division)
subcategory: State capital expenditure financing
period: Annual iterations since FY2020-21; FY2026-27 guidelines issued 27 March 2026 (F.No. 44(1)/PF-S/2026-27 (CAPEX)); cumulative allocations Rs 5.3+ lakh crore since inception.
whyItMatters: SASCI is the single largest flexible capital-investment channel available to Sikkim - a 50-year INTEREST-FREE LOAN (not a grant) over and above normal borrowing limits. The FY2026-27 iteration earmarks Rs 75,000 crore under Part-I alone, of which Rs 67,000 crore goes to states in proportion to their 16th Finance Commission tax-devolution share - Sikkim's share flows automatically once it submits eligible projects. Further reform/incentive-linked parts (public finance IT, mining, AgriStack, livestock, financial management, compressed biogas, and an earmarked health-infrastructure component) are issued separately. Sikkim has already used the SASCI tourism window (Bhaleydhunga skywalk, Nathu La border experience).
eligibleApplicants: State Governments only (Finance Departments submit consolidated proposals)
sikkimNodalDept: Finance Department, Government of Sikkim (with Planning & Development Department for project pipeline)
whatCanBeFunded: New and ongoing capital investment projects across sectors (Part-I largely untied); earlier/parallel windows have covered tourism (iconic centres), urban planning reforms, industrial estates, and sector reforms; FY2026-27 incentive parts tied to specified reforms; a health-infrastructure earmark exists per state-level reporting.
fundingAvailable: FY2026-27 Part-I: Rs 75,000 crore national (Rs 67,000 crore for states by 16th FC tax share; Rs 3,000 crore for UTs with legislature; Rs 5,000 crore for balance releases of approved projects). Remaining parts notified separately. Sikkim's FY2026-27 entitlement: Not confirmed from available official guidance.
fundingRatio: 100% central loan for approved capital projects (no state matching share; loan repayable in year 50, interest-free).
nePreferenceDetail: Allocation follows Finance Commission tax-devolution shares (which embed area/forest weights that benefit Sikkim); no separate NE quota confirmed in the FY2026-27 guidelines.
stateContribution: None for eligible project costs; state bears repayment liability after 50 years and must meet scheme conditions (capex utilisation timelines, project standards, single nodal account discipline - details per guidelines).

name: 16th Finance Commission tax devolution (states' share of the divisible pool), award period 2026-27 to 2030-31
agency: Department of Expenditure / Department of Economic Affairs (FC Division); Sixteenth Finance Commission (fincomindia.nic.in)
subcategory: Vertical and horizontal tax devolution
period: 2026-27 to 2030-31 (report submitted late 2025; tabled in Lok Sabha with Budget on 1 February 2026)
whyItMatters: Tax devolution is the single largest untied resource in Sikkim's budget and the foundation on which everything else (including its SASCI Part-I entitlement, now keyed to the 16th FC share) is built. The 16th FC retained the vertical share at 41% but changed the horizontal formula — notably adding a 10% weight for contribution to GDP and removing the tax-effort criterion — changes that plausibly work against a tiny-GSDP state like Sikkim, making it essential to know the new inter-se share precisely. Under the 15th FC Sikkim's share was 0.388% of the states' pool; the 16th FC share for Sikkim is not yet confirmed in this research. With revenue deficit grants discontinued, devolution is now even more decisively Sikkim's fiscal lifeline.
eligibleApplicants: All States (constitutional entitlement under Articles 270/280 — no application)
sikkimNodalDept: Finance Department (FRED) — Budget and Resource Division
whatCanBeFunded: Fully untied — general budgetary resources of the State
fundingAvailable: 41% of the divisible pool of central taxes devolved to states for 2026-31 (vertical share retained from the 15th FC). Sikkim's inter-se share under the 16th FC: Not confirmed from available official guidance (15th FC comparator: 0.388% of the states' share).
nePreferenceDetail: No NE-specific weight; however, formula components such as income distance, area and forest/ecology have historically favoured Sikkim relative to population (16th FC weights not fully confirmed)
stateContribution: None
accessPathway: No application — devolution flows automatically in instalments (typically monthly, with year-end adjustment) to the State Consolidated Fund

Re-cast Sikkim's medium-term fiscal projections (FY27-FY31) on the new share, since the discontinuation of revenue deficit grants changes the revenue account outlook
Track monthly devolution releases (PIB/DoE release orders) against budget estimates
nextAction: FRED's Budget Division should extract Sikkim's 2026-31 inter-se share from the 16th FC report (fincomindia.nic.in / Budget 2026-27 documents) and rebase the state's FY27-FY31 receipts forecast this quarter.

name: NABARD Rural Infrastructure Development Fund
agency: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)
subcategory: Concessional loans to state governments
period: Continuous since 1995-96 (initial corpus Rs 2,000 crore); a new tranche is announced each financial year in the Union Budget - FY2026-27 tranche size not confirmed from available official guidance
whyItMatters: RIDF is Sikkim's most accessible concessional borrowing window for exactly the assets this cluster needs - rural roads and bridges across dispersed hill settlements, minor irrigation channels, rural drinking water works, soil conservation, schools and health sub-centres (39 eligible activities). Sikkim enjoys explicit NE preference: RIDF finances 90% of eligible project cost for social sector and rural connectivity projects from NE states and Sikkim (versus lower shares elsewhere), minimising upfront state outlay. This is a loan repaid by the state, routed through the Finance Department against the state's borrowing plan, so project selection should prioritise assets with high economic returns or O&M savings.
eligibleApplicants: State Government of Sikkim (line departments through the Finance Department)
State-owned corporations (with state guarantee)
sikkimNodalDept: Finance Department, Government of Sikkim (nodal for RIDF borrowing), with Rural Development, Roads & Bridges, Water Resources and PHE Departments as project departments
whatCanBeFunded: 39 GoI-approved activities across three broad sectors: agriculture and related (minor/micro irrigation, soil conservation, watershed, flood protection, cold chains, rural markets), social sector (drinking water, sanitation, schools, anganwadis, health infrastructure), and rural connectivity (rural roads and bridges).
fundingAvailable: Annual national tranche announced in the Union Budget (fund has grown far beyond the initial Rs 2,000 crore corpus; recent tranches have been in the tens of thousands of crores - FY2026-27 figure not confirmed). Sikkim's drawal is limited by its approved projects and state borrowing headroom, not a fixed quota (state-wise normative allocation practice requires confirmation).

nePreferenceDetail: For projects from NE states and Sikkim (and hill states of HP, J&K, Uttarakhand), RIDF assistance is 90% of eligible project cost in the social sector and rural connectivity sectors.
stateContribution: Minimum ~10% of project cost for the preferential sectors (balance of eligible cost), plus debt-service obligations; interest rate and 7-year-style repayment terms as per prevailing NABARD circulars (exact current rate: Not confirmed from available official guidance).

Finance Department (nodal) prioritises projects within the state's annual RIDF borrowing plan and fiscal/borrowing limits, and forwards proposals to NABARD's Sikkim Regional Office, Gangtok.
NABARD appraises (techno-financial) and sanctions projects tranche-wise; a loan agreement is executed with the State Government.
Funds released largely as reimbursement against expenditure (with mobilisation advance per norms - requires confirmation); departments execute and report physical/financial progress.
Finance Department services the loan; completed-project returns and utilisation drive future sanction headroom.
nextAction: The Sikkim Finance Department should convene line departments to assemble the FY2027-28 RIDF project shelf (rural bridges, minor irrigation, drinking-water source works) and lodge DPRs with NABARD Regional Office Gangtok before the tranche programming cycle.

period: 15th FC award (2021-26) was the last to carry revenue deficit grants; the 16th FC (2026-31) has recommended none
whyItMatters: The disappearance of revenue deficit grants is the biggest negative fiscal-transfer development for special-category and hill states in the 16th FC award, and Sikkim's own memorandum to the Commission had sought such support. Sikkim must now absorb any post-devolution revenue gap through own-revenue effort, expenditure rationalisation or the (larger) untied devolution pool — there is no gap-filling grant to fall back on for 2026-31. This record exists so the Finance Department treats the discontinuation as a planning fact, not an application opportunity.
eligibleApplicants: No state — instrument discontinued for 2026-31
sikkimNodalDept: Finance Department (FRED)
whatCanBeFunded: Historically: untied support to the revenue account of states with assessed post-devolution revenue deficits. For 2026-31: nothing — instrument discontinued.
fundingAvailable: Nil for 2026-31. Under the 15th FC, revenue deficit grants went to 17 states in 2021-22 tapering over the award; whether and how much Sikkim received in any year of the 15th FC award: Not confirmed from available official guidance.
nePreferenceDetail: Commentary notes NE and hill states are the group most affected by the discontinuation
stateContribution: n/a
accessPathway: No pathway — the 16th FC recommended discontinuation of revenue deficit grants (along with sector-specific and state-specific grants)
FRED should verify from the Action Taken Report/Explanatory Memorandum with Budget 2026-27 that the Government accepted the discontinuation without transitional relief (requires confirmation)

If a genuine structural revenue gap emerges, the remaining avenues are representations for special assistance outside the FC framework and NEC/DoNER channels (separate cluster) — there is no FC application route
nextAction: FRED should confirm from the Budget 2026-27 Explanatory Memorandum whether any transitional or substitute support accompanies the RD-grant discontinuation, and quantify Sikkim's unfunded revenue gap for FY27-FY31.

name: National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM)

period: Approved January 2023; outlay ₹19,744 crore up to 2029-30

Sikkim's relevance is as a renewable (hydro) power source for green hydrogen and as a possible site for small mobility/decentralised pilots; designated hydrogen hubs are in other states. name: Legacy Special Plan Assistance (SPA) / Special Central Assistance (SCA) / Normal Central Assistance (NCA) to Special Category States — status check
agency: Department of Expenditure
subcategory: Discontinued plan assistance instruments
period: Operated until FY 2014-15/2015-16; subsumed after the 14th Finance Commission award and abolition of the Planning Commission
whyItMatters: Sikkim, as a Special Category State, historically received untied NCA on the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula (90% grant) plus SPA/SCA top-ups — instruments that older project documents and departmental expectations in Gangtok still occasionally reference. Nothing of this architecture remains: the 14th FC folded plan assistance into higher devolution, and today's functional successors are SASCI (capital loans), FC grants, NEC/NESIDS and DoNER schemes. This record exists to prevent effort being spent chasing a channel that no longer exists and to redirect legacy expectations to the live instruments.
eligibleApplicants: None — discontinued
sikkimNodalDept: Finance Department (FRED) / Development Planning, Economic Reforms & NEC Affairs Department (for legacy reconciliation)
whatCanBeFunded: Nothing new. Legacy task only: reconciling any unreconciled SPA/SCA-era project balances or UCs in state books.
fundingAvailable: Nil
nePreferenceDetail: Historically 90:10 grant-heavy terms for special category states — the lineage of today's NE preferences in CSS ratios and EAP pass-through
stateContribution: n/a
accessPathway: No access — instrument discontinued; any residual SPA/SCA balances in Sikkim's books should be reconciled and closed with AG (Accounts) (requires confirmation whether any remain)
Redirect legacy 'special assistance' asks to SASCI (capital), Pride of Hills window, FC-XVI grants, NEC/NESIDS and DoNER channels
nextAction: FRED should run a one-time ledger check with the Accountant General for any unclosed SPA/SCA-era balances and formally retire the heads, redirecting departmental proposals to SASCI and DoNER channels.
